verdicts.title: Cantique (Laetare anima mea), Op. 77 No. 1
verdicts.note: Title confirmed: BIS Sibelius Edition vol. 6 booklet 'I. Cantique (Laetare anima mea)' 5'23; IMSLP 'Laetare anima mea'; Wikipedia 'Cantique'. Only the set name is wrong: the opus is 'Two Serious Melodies' (Zwei ernste Melodien), not 'Two Pieces'. Violin & orchestra (Wilhelm Hansen 1922) plus violin & piano version by Sibelius (Hansen 1923), so 'Piano or orchestra' is right. Same set rename applies to N3.

verdicts.title: Devotion (Ab imo pectore), Op. 77 No. 2
verdicts.note: (verify:false, checked anyway) Title confirmed (BIS booklet 'II. Devotion (Ab imo pectore)', IMSLP, Wikipedia). Set renamed as for N2. Duration is 3'01 on BIS (whole opus about 8 min), not 6.

verdicts.title: Romance in B minor, Op. 2 No. 1
verdicts.note: Exists as titled: IMSLP '2 Pieces for Violin and Piano, Op.2' (Universal Edition 1912, no. 1 'Romanze', rev. 1911); Wikipedia work list 'Romance, Op. 2/1, B minor'; BIS booklet 'Romance in B minor. Grave' 3'06. Only change: minutes 4 -> 3.

verdicts.title: Epilogue, Op. 2 No. 2
verdicts.note: 'Perpetuum mobile' is the title of the 1891 ORIGINAL version (BIS appendix 'Two Pieces, Op. 2 (original versions)': Perpetuum mobile, Vivace, 1'30, Nuori Suomi). The published 1911 revision (Universal Edition 1912) is 'Epilog'/'Epilogue', Allegro, 2'37 on BIS; IMSLP lists 'Perpetuum mobile (1888), Epilog (1911)'; Wikipedia 'Epilog (Epilogue)'. So drop the parenthesis. Minutes 4 -> 3.

verdicts.title: Impromptu, Op. 78 No. 1
verdicts.note: (verify:false) Title confirmed by BIS booklet (Four Pieces, Op. 78, Wilhelm Hansen: Impromptu, Romance in F major, Religioso, Rigaudon). Impromptu is 1'40, so minutes 3 -> 2.

verdicts.title: Rigaudon, Op. 78 No. 4
verdicts.note: (verify:false) Title confirmed by BIS booklet. Rigaudon is 1'52, so minutes 3 -> 2.

verdicts.title: Auf der Heide (On the Heath), Op. 115 No. 1
verdicts.note: (verify:false) Title confirmed by Breitkopf & Härtel catalogue ('Auf der Heide (On the Heath)'). BIS: Andantino 2'21 (whole of Op. 115 is about 10 min, not 15), so minutes 4 -> 2.

verdicts.title: Ballade, Op. 115 No. 2
verdicts.note: (verify:false) Title confirmed (Breitkopf, BIS). Allegro moderato 3'54, so minutes 5 -> 4.

verdicts.title: Humoresque, Op. 115 No. 3
verdicts.note: (verify:false) Title confirmed (Breitkopf, BIS 'Humoresque. Tranquillo - Allegretto' 2'15). Minutes 3 -> 2.

verdicts.title: Die Glocken (The Bells), Op. 115 No. 4
verdicts.note: German title is the original (first edition Breitkopf & Härtel 1930): Breitkopf catalogue 'Die Glocken (The Bells)', Wikipedia 'Four Pieces, Op. 115' same, BIS 'IV. Die Glocken (Capriccietto). Presto' 1'20. IMSLP gives only 'The Bells'. Reordered to match N9 pattern. Minutes 3 -> 1.

verdicts.title: Scène de danse, Op. 116 No. 1
verdicts.note: (verify:false) Title confirmed by BIS booklet (Three Pieces, Op. 116, Breitkopf & Härtel 1929: Scène de danse, Danse caractéristique, Rondeau romantique). Scène de danse 2'06, so minutes 3 -> 2. Nos. 14 and 15 are fine (2'40, 4'20).

(verify:false) IMSLP: Op.117 = JS 185, 1929, Allegretto / Andantino / Vivace ('Country Scenery', 'Serenade: Evening in Spring', 'In the Summer'), about 8 min, first published K.G. Fazer 1993. IMSLP lists NO arrangements, so a piano reduction is unconfirmed; if none is published the accompaniment should be 'Strings'.
(verify:false) IMSLP lists a violin and piano arrangement by Friedrich Hermann (1828-1907), Breitkopf & Härtel 1907, plate V.A. 2283. It is the only violin arrangement of Valse triste listed.

Wikipedia work list: 'Serenade No. 1 in D major, Op. 69a (1912)'. IMSLP: Op.69 (IJS 83) '2 Serenades for Violin and Orchestra', 1912-13, Breitkopf & Härtel 1913, about 15 min in total; violin & piano reduction by Hermann Gärtner (B&H 1913, plates E.B. 3936-37). Note: existing id 64 'Two Serenades, Op. 69' is the set entry for the same two pieces.
Wikipedia work list: 'Serenade No. 2 in G minor, Op. 69b (1912-1913)'. Same IMSLP page and Gärtner piano reduction as N18.

Exists: Violin Sonata in F major, JS 178 (1889), 3 movements (Allegro / Andante / Vivace). Published by Fennica Gehrman (Schott order no. F 1000853, 52 pp.); recorded on BIS (Kuusisto/Gräsbeck, BIS-CD-1915/17: 11'09 + 5'57 + 7'52 = 25'14; also BIS-CD-1023). 25 min is right; a 25-minute early-Romantic sonata may deserve level 6 rather than 5.

gaps.title: Scène d'amour, Op. 71 (from Scaramouche)
gaps.scoring: violin and piano, arranged by Sibelius himself from the ballet-pantomime Scaramouche (1913)
gaps.note: Also in BIS Sibelius Edition vol. 6 (Sparf/Forsberg, 6'10, 'Lento - Andantino - Cantabile', credited Wilhelm Hansen). Not in existing or queued.

gaps.title: Suite in E major, JS 188
gaps.scoring: violin and piano, 4 movements (Allegro molto moderato - quasi adagio / Allegro molto / Più lento quasi andantino / Allegro brillante), 1888
gaps.edition: Warner/Chappell Music Finland (the credit printed in the BIS booklet; not independently checked in a current publisher catalogue)
gaps.note: Recorded by Kuusisto/Gräsbeck (BIS; 17'21). Publication evidence is the BIS source credit only (works with no published edition are credited 'M/s ...' there). Include only if the owner accepts that evidence. Other early JS-numbered violin works (Sonata in A minor JS 177, Suite in D minor JS 187, Duo in C major JS 66, En glad musikant JS 70, Lullaby JS 222 for violin and kantele) are credited as manuscripts or have no ordinary published edition, so they were NOT proposed.

existing_issues.issue: Title lacks key and minutes are high: Op. 78 No. 2 is Romance in F major (revised 1915), 3'22 on BIS (minutes 4 -> 3).
existing_issues.suggested_title: Romance in F major, Op. 78 No. 2

existing_issues.issue: Set entry minutes 12 is too low: the five Danses champêtres total 16'21 on BIS (4'11 + 2'07 + 3'53 + 2'55 + 2'57), so minutes should be about 16.
Minutes 11 is low: Sonatina in E major, Op. 80 runs 12'51 on BIS (3'49 + 3'51 + 3'58), so about 13.
